import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('data/FUN_company_pl_actuals_dataset.csv')

# Part 1: Year with best revenue
revenue_by_year = df[df['FSLine Statement L1'] == 'Net Revenue'].groupby('Fiscal Year')['Amount in USD'].sum()
print('=== Net Revenue by Year ===')
print(revenue_by_year.sort_values(ascending=False))
print()
best_revenue_year = revenue_by_year.idxmax()
print(f'Year with BEST revenue: {best_revenue_year} (\\${revenue_by_year[best_revenue_year]:,.2f})')

print()
print('='*50)
print()

# Part 2: Year with worst product
# I'll interpret this as: for each year, which product had the lowest revenue, 
# and which year had the overall worst-performing product
revenue_by_year_product = df[df['FSLine Statement L1'] == 'Net Revenue'].groupby(['Fiscal Year', 'Product'])['Amount in USD'].sum().reset_index()

print('=== Revenue by Year and Product ===')
print(revenue_by_year_product.pivot(index='Product', columns='Fiscal Year', values='Amount in USD').to_string())
print()

# Find the minimum revenue product for each year
min_by_year = revenue_by_year_product.loc[revenue_by_year_product.groupby('Fiscal Year')['Amount in USD'].idxmin()]
print('=== Worst Product by Year ===')
print(min_by_year)
print()

# Find the overall worst (lowest revenue entry)
worst_row = revenue_by_year_product.loc[revenue_by_year_product['Amount in USD'].idxmin()]
print(f'Year with WORST product: {worst_row[\"Fiscal Year\"]} - Product: {worst_row[\"Product\"]} (\\${worst_row[\"Amount in USD\"]:,.2f})')
"
